result: Three-base nucleic acid sequences (AUC for RNA, ATG/ATC for DNA) are intrinsically unstructured with positive free energies of self-folding and hybridize at exceptionally fast rates (~10^7 M^-1s^-1) without compromising sequence specificity, as demonstrated by computational analysis and experimental measurements.
evaluation: Reviewers praised the probe design work as 'impressive' and noted 'the general idea of removing internal structures with individual oligos to accelerate annealing, and in particular using three nucleotides only, will also have a broad appeal.' The technical quality was described as 'high' with 'clear' data, indicating acceptance of these foundational claims about three-base probe design.

result: FastFISH probes F1 and F2 anneal to their RNA targets at rates of 6×10^6 and 4×10^6 M^-1s^-1 respectively, which are at least 100-fold faster than typical four-base probes. Introducing G residues progressively decreases hybridization rates (10-fold for one G, 300-fold for four G residues), correlating with lower free energies of self-folding.
evaluation: Reviewers stated 'It is clear from the data that their probe design makes the DNA annealing 100 fold faster for probes about 20 nt long' and described the technical quality as 'high' with 'clear' data. The experimental demonstration of the relationship between structure and hybridization rate was accepted without challenge.

result: Three-letter 19-mer sequences have complexity indices of 8.1±0.8 compared to 9.3±0.8 for four-letter sequences, with ~31% of three-letter sequences having complexity indices ≥9 that match or exceed the average complexity of human exons (8.9±1.0).
evaluation: Reviewers requested clarification about the complexity index, stating 'The description of the complexity index is not straightforward to understand (what does "by cutting and insertion" mean exactly; cutting of what, where, and insertion of what?).' This indicates the reviewers found the presentation unclear, though they did not reject the underlying claim.

result: Self-quenching of fastFISH probes enables the use of free probes at concentrations up to 1 μM, likely mediated by random polymer motion and/or contact quenching rather than hairpin formation.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the self-quenching mechanism or its effectiveness. The overall assessment that 'the technical quality of the work is high, and the data are clear' implicitly supports these claims about probe design and function.

result: RNAP-DNA binding events comprise two populations: short-lived events (T0~0.14s) representing non-productive RPc/RPo, and long-lived events (T1~1.7s) representing full transcription cycles, with peak dwell time increasing linearly with DNA length.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the interpretation, stating 'This statement is premature since abortive initiation was not addressed. At this stage of the paper, the long lived complexes might have derived from abortive initiation.' They suggested 'perhaps this information could be included and discussed in Figure 3D,' indicating the evidence was incomplete at this stage of the manuscript.

result: The RNAP elongation rate is ~300 nt s^-1 based on dwell time vs DNA length analysis. The net stationary time (Tstationary) is 0.7±0.3s, and the duration of abortive cycling (Tabortive) is ~0.2s, calculated from the time delay between RNAP and probe arrival (ΔTon=0.7±0.2s).
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged 'the direct observation of various stages of transcription starting from RNAP binding until its dissociation from the transcript has established important benchmarks for future studies.' The kinetic measurements were accepted as valid, though reviewers noted the biological system (T7 RNAP) was well-studied.

result: FastFISH achieves ~81% efficiency in detecting nascent RNA, with probe and RNAP dissociating simultaneously in ~72% of cases. Probe binding is specific to nascent RNA (not RNAP or DNA), requires transcription beyond position +6, and is delayed by ~0.5s when the target is moved 153 bp downstream.
evaluation: Reviewers stated 'the production of the mRNA can be detected with high confidence with minimal false negatives' and noted 'the fastFISH approach was absolutely necessary for this work because the overall duration of the reaction was about 1–2 s and any slower annealing would have missed the majority of events.' The specificity controls were implicitly accepted.

result: RNAP might dwell at the end of the DNA template for ~0.5s before run-off, a phenomenon previously observed with bacterial and eukaryotic polymerases involving backtracking.
evaluation: Reviewers specifically requested citation of this phenomenon: 'It is known (published) that bacterial and eukaryotic polymerases are slow to release from the ends of DNA during runoff transcription. This may also be true for T7RNAP. If such results are published, it would be best to cite the work on this phenomenon to avoid the appearance of inventing an ad hoc explanation for the data.' This indicates acceptance of the observation once properly contextualized.

result: The measured rates of RPc dissociation (koff~3 s^-1), promoter escape (kescape~5 s^-1), and elongation (~300 nt s^-1) are higher than previous studies, likely due to the use of optimal physiological temperature (37°C) where T7 RNAP catalytic rate increases up to 10-fold compared to 20°C.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the faster rates, noting 'the direct observation of various stages of transcription...has established important benchmarks for future studies.' The temperature explanation was not challenged, and the overall assessment was that 'the technical quality of the work is high, and the data are clear.'

result: Specific probe-DNA interactions were observed with wild type but not null mutant promoters. In typical experiments, 10-30% of DNA templates co-localized with probe, with incomplete utilization likely due to surface interference rather than inefficient probe hybridization.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the specificity controls or the interpretation of incomplete template utilization. The overall positive assessment of technical quality and data clarity indicates acceptance of these foundational experimental observations.

result: Hybridization requires unfolding of nucleic acid fragments into unstructured coils followed by base-pairing. Probes with less stable secondary structures show faster hybridization rates, and decreasing hairpin length in molecular beacons increases hybridization rates.
evaluation: Reviewers found the discussion confusing, stating 'This is confusing and is possibly just mis-written. Taken to the extreme it is obviously untrue. A long, perfectly matched hairpin will essentially not melt spontaneously and allow for strand invasion. Please clarify.' They also noted 'Overall this discussion does not do a great job of separating the discussion of rate-limiting effects (unfolding vs base-pairing with target...).'

result: The dwell time distribution of productive RNAP-DNA interactions was skewed toward longer events, likely due to spontaneous RNAP pausing, which might explain previously reported premature dissociation of colliding RNAPs at high RNAP:template ratios.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the observation of pausing or its interpretation. The overall positive assessment of the work and the statement that it 'established important benchmarks for future studies' indicates acceptance of these observations about RNAP dynamics.

result: FastFISH achieves exceptionally fast hybridization rates (~10^7 M^-1s^-1) by using intrinsically unstructured nucleic acid sequences, allows deterministic detection of single nascent transcripts, and can measure kinetic rates of promoter escape, elongation, and termination at sub-second temporal resolution.
evaluation: Reviewers described this as 'an outstanding paper' and stated 'fastFISH will be useful for the single-molecule analysis not only of general transcription machineries but also of other RNA modifying enzymes.' They emphasized 'the fastFISH approach was absolutely necessary for this work because the overall duration of the reaction was about 1–2 s and any slower annealing would have missed the majority of events.'

result: The principles of fastFISH design can be applied to study stochasticity in gene regulation, select targets for gene silencing, design nucleic acid nanostructures, detect endogenous RNAs in situ and in vivo, and study dynamics of multi-subunit RNAPs and RNA-processing events.
evaluation: Reviewers stated 'the general idea of removing internal structures with individual oligos to accelerate annealing, and in particular using three nucleotides only, will also have a broad appeal' and noted the method 'will be useful for the single-molecule analysis not only of general transcription machineries but also of other RNA modifying enzymes.' This indicates acceptance of the broad applicability claims.

result: The durations of observed RNAP-DNA interactions were not limited by Cy5 photobleaching, and protein labeling efficiencies of Cy5-Halo-RNAP were >90% based on UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy.
evaluation: Reviewers requested clarification about the fusion protein: 'It should be clearly stated in the main text that the T7RNAP used for most of the experiments is a fusion protein. I believe the halo tag is ∼34 kDa.' They also requested additional controls: 'It would also be good to include the unlabeled halo tagged RNAP in this figure to see if the N-terminal tag itself has some detrimental effect.'
